title: What If Earth Lost Its Magnetic Field?

scenes.text: What if Earth's magnetic field vanished tomorrow? The sky would light up first.
The northern and southern lights would appear much closer to the equator, as charged particles from the Sun reach lower latitudes.
Compasses would stop pointing reliably north, and more solar particles would disrupt power grids and satellites.
The solar wind could slowly strip away our air. Mars lost its field about four billion years ago, and most of its atmosphere with it.
More ultraviolet radiation would reach the ground, raising skin cancer risk. Still, scientists say life would probably survive the short term.
The field isn't expected to vanish for billions of years. Even the last reversal, about 780,000 years ago, never switched it off.
